title: Patna and Nanded
hook: he funded buildings at the Tenth Guru's birthplace and resting place

segments.voice: Yesterday, few executions, and your line was mercy in power. Where did you choose mercy, even once? Today, the Maharaja's gifts travel a very long way from Lahore. Day nine hundred twenty-two.

Draw a line on a map of India. Start at Patna, on the Ganges, far to the east. Follow it a long way south and west, down into the Deccan, to Nanded, on the Godavari river. Neither city is in the Punjab. Neither was in Ranjit Singh's kingdom. Yet his money went to both, to build and adorn places that Sikhs travel to. One is where the Tenth Guru was born. The other is where his earthly life ended. Today: Patna and Nanded.
screen: `PATNA, ON THE GANGES.` → `NANDED, ON THE GODAVARI.` → `FAR OUTSIDE HIS KINGDOM.`

segments.voice: First, Patna. Guru Gobind Singh was born there, while his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was traveling in the east. The child spent his early years in Patna before the family came to Anandpur. The place of his birth became a gurdwara, and today it's one of the Takhts, the seats of authority Sikhs honor. Second, Nanded. At the end of his life, Guru Gobind Singh traveled south to the Deccan, and it was at Nanded that he gave the Guruship to the Granth and left this world. Sikhs call the gurdwara there Hazur Sahib, and it too is a Takht. Third, the gifts. Histories and gurdwara tradition say Ranjit Singh sent money and craftsmen to both places, to raise and beautify the buildings. He had already covered the Harmandir in gold at Amritsar, inside his own kingdom. These gifts went far beyond his borders, to places he would never rule. That's the point of them. They weren't about holding land. They were about honoring the Guru. And fourth, the line it draws. The Tenth Guru's life ran from the Ganges to the Godavari. A Maharaja in Lahore sent his gifts along that same line, east and south, joining the Punjab to the places where the Guru's life began and ended. Sikhs still travel that line today, and tradition says some of what they see there was paid for from Lahore.
screen: `PATNA, WHERE THE TENTH GURU WAS BORN.` · `NANDED, WHERE HIS EARTHLY LIFE ENDED.` · `GIFTS BEYOND THE KINGDOM'S BORDERS.` · `A LINE FROM THE GANGES TO THE GODAVARI.` · then, large: `GIFTS TO THE GURU'S PLACES.`

segments.voice: Two minutes with a sacred place. Sit, and let your breath grow slow. Bring to mind a place that's holy to you, or to someone you love: a gurdwara, a church, a temple, a grave, a tree, a kitchen where someone prayed. Picture it clearly. Now think of one small gift you could give it: a few coins, an hour of cleaning, flowers, a visit, a word of thanks to whoever keeps it. Just choose it. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Patna and Nanded. The Tenth Guru's birthplace on the Ganges and his resting place on the Godavari, both far from Lahore, both honored with the Maharaja's gifts. Today's word.
Your line: gifts to the guru's places. Today, give the small gift you chose to a sacred place, near or far. Day nine hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Sikhs travel to Takht Sri Patna Sahib and Takht Sri Hazur Sahib at Nanded, the places of Guru Gobind Singh's birth and his final days, and give donations there.
